title: Becoming a self-regulated learner: An overview
decision_use: Separates forethought, performance and self-reflection; supports representing goal, planning, monitoring and reflection independently.
limits: Not a product evaluation and does not prescribe digital parameter defaults.

title: A Review of Self-regulated Learning: Six Models and Four Directions for Research
decision_use: SRL includes cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, behavioral and affective processes; prevents one monolithic self-regulation parameter.
limits: Model comparison, not evidence that every subprocess should be implemented.

title: Self-regulated learning strategies & academic achievement in online higher education learning environments: A systematic review
decision_use: Supports explicit planning, time/effort regulation, metacognition and critical thinking candidates while retaining context limits.
limits: Correlational evidence dominates; higher education and pre-2015 online contexts.

title: How can primary school students learn self-regulated learning strategies most effectively?
decision_use: Supports explicit SRL instruction and multiple strategy families rather than assuming learner control creates self-regulation.
limits: School-age populations; intervention features do not directly map to software parameters.

title: Components of fostering self-regulated learning among students
decision_use: Supports decomposing cognitive, metacognitive and motivational support and retaining educational-level moderators.
limits: Older interventions; no claim that prompts or dashboards alone reproduce interventions.

title: Updated Meta-Analysis of Learner Control Within Educational Technology
decision_use: Near-zero overall academic effect argues against unlimited control as a universal default and for separating control dimensions.
limits: Heterogeneous and older educational technology; does not evaluate current LLM interfaces.

title: Effects of Students’ Autonomy Support on their Self-Regulated Learning Strategies: Three Field Experiments in Secondary Education
decision_use: Supports autonomy-support as designed structure rather than abandonment and motivates shared-control profiles.
limits: Secondary schools and intervention-specific measures.

title: Exploring shared control in upper primary school learners working with an adaptive learning technology
decision_use: Provides a current implemented example in which learners adjust difficulty while the system selects tasks; supports separating human and system authority.
limits: Recent, narrow population and domain; not evidence for general adaptive defaults.

title: Toward Meta-cognitive Tutoring: A Model of Help Seeking with a Cognitive Tutor
decision_use: Supports distinguishing availability of help, learner request, hint abuse, feedback on help-seeking and metacognitive goals.
limits: Rule-based tutor and domain-specific model; should not become automatic surveillance of help behavior.

title: Improving students’ help-seeking skills using metacognitive feedback in an intelligent tutoring system
decision_use: Supports optional metacognitive feedback and help-seeking instruction while separating learning support from punitive interpretation.
limits: Specific ITS and population; automated feedback depends on validated behavioral model.

title: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Learning Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis
decision_use: ITS can improve outcomes versus several controls but effects depend on comparisons; adaptation is a capability family, not a universal mechanism.
limits: Pre-generative-AI ITS; broad heterogeneity and publication-era constraints.

title: A Meta-Analysis of Moderators of the Effects of Technology-Enhanced Adaptive Learning on Primary and Secondary Students' Learning Outcomes
decision_use: Current evidence supports moderator-sensitive treatment of adaptive learning and separate cognitive, affective and behavioral outcomes.
limits: School populations and studies from 2012–2021; does not validate any ARA adaptation algorithm.

title: AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting
decision_use: Shows potential of carefully designed AI tutoring and supports function-specific, research-grounded AI profiles.
limits: Custom tutor, selected content, one institution/domain and short intervention; not evidence for general autonomous AI.

title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
decision_use: AI can improve practice performance while reducing unaided acquisition; motivates guardrails, cognitive effort preservation and no automatic answer substitution.
limits: Mathematics and specific GPT-4 interfaces; guardrails and outcomes may not generalize.

title: Disclosures & Disclaimers: Investigating the Impact of Transparency Disclosures and Reliability Disclaimers on Learner-LLM Interactions
decision_use: Disclaimers may reduce overreliance and prompt/system transparency affects confidence and behavior; transparency must be parameterized by purpose.
limits: Single assignment and tutor; disclosures did not uniformly improve performance.

title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
decision_use: Supports communicating capability limits, supporting correction, scope-aware explanation, feedback, control and graceful failure.
limits: General HAI guidelines; educational validity requires domain-specific adaptation.

title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making
decision_use: Explanations alone do not ensure appropriate reliance; active review or prediction-before-AI can reduce overreliance with usability trade-offs.
limits: Decision tasks outside education and subgroup moderation; forcing should not become universal friction.

title: Cognitive Forcing for Better Decision-Making: Reducing Overreliance on AI Systems Through Partial Explanations
decision_use: Supports configurable partial explanations and reflection prompts rather than assuming full explanations are safest.
limits: Non-educational tasks; partial explanations can create workload and accessibility concerns.

title: Overcoming Algorithm Aversion: People Will Use Imperfect Algorithms If They Can (Even Slightly) Modify Them
decision_use: Supports editability and bounded override as adoption and control mechanisms for AI-generated recommendations.
limits: Forecasting context; user modification can also reduce quality and needs provenance.

title: Automation Bias in AI-Decision Support: Results from an Empirical Study
decision_use: Human oversight is vulnerable to false agreement, especially among non-specialists; supports training, inspectability and non-authoritative defaults.
limits: Clinical task and demographic effects; transfer to education is inferential.

title: Understanding the Impact of Human Oversight on Discriminatory Outcomes in AI-Supported Decision-Making
decision_use: Human-in-the-loop does not by itself correct biased AI; supports systemic controls, role training and explicit override guidance.
limits: Consequential employment/lending decisions, not educational authoring.

title: Universal Design for Learning Guidelines version 3.0
decision_use: Supports designing multiple means of engagement, representation, action/expression and learner agency while addressing systemic barriers.
limits: Framework, not a product-effect estimate; implementation must remain goal- and construct-aware.

title: UDL Guidelines 3.0: A Community-Driven, Research-Based Process Toward Fulfilling the Promise of Universal Design for Learning
decision_use: Supports treating accessibility and learner variability as design inputs and involving affected users in validation.
limits: Process report; does not define ARA parameters or conformance.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
decision_use: Provides testable baseline for perceivable, operable, understandable and robust interfaces across desktop and mobile.
limits: Does not cover every cognitive/accessibility need and does not define pedagogical equivalence.

title: The effectiveness of universal design for learning: A systematic review of the literature and meta-analysis
decision_use: Supports retaining UDL as evidence-informed design family while avoiding claims that one implementation is universally effective.
limits: Heterogeneous interventions and quality; UDL components are inconsistently operationalized.

title: A Systematic Literature Review on the Effectiveness of Universal Design for Learning in Second-Level Education
decision_use: Finds positive academic/social signals but less implementation of autonomy and self-regulation; supports explicit P3 integration.
limits: Young evidence base and heterogeneous mainstream-school interventions.

title: AI for Students with Learning Disabilities: A Systematic Review
decision_use: Shows accessibility opportunities but narrow condition coverage; supports disability-specific validation and no universal AI accommodation.
limits: Ten of sixteen studies concern dyslexia; limited evidence for other disabilities.

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Reality on Educational Inclusion
decision_use: Supports possible personalization and assistive functions while requiring inclusion, accessibility, social and implementation evaluation.
limits: Combines AI and VR and heterogeneous studies; evidence quality and long-term outcomes vary.

title: Guidance for generative AI in education and research
decision_use: Supports human-centred, age/role-appropriate, privacy-protective, validated and capacity-building use of GenAI.
limits: Guidance, not empirical proof; jurisdiction-specific rules remain separate.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
decision_use: Supports continuous govern-map-measure-manage lifecycle, documentation of intended use, affected actors, risks and monitoring.
limits: Cross-sector framework; not an educational product specification and currently under revision.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
decision_use: Supports risk documentation for confabulation, data privacy, human-AI configuration, provenance, content integrity and evaluation.
limits: Not education-specific and does not determine product defaults.

title: The Learner Control Principle in Multimedia Learning
decision_use: Supports conditional learner control, advisement and expertise-sensitive design rather than unlimited options.
limits: Chapter synthesis and multimedia focus; not current AI authoring.

title: An effective metacognitive strategy: learning by doing and explaining with a computer-based Cognitive Tutor
decision_use: Supports self-explanation as an optional learning operation and distinguishes AI answer production from prompts that preserve learner reasoning.
limits: Geometry and rule-based tutor; natural-language LLM assistance differs.

title: Effectiveness of a generative AI-powered digital tutor integrated with a knowledge graph in anatomy education for nursing students
decision_use: Current evidence for blended GenAI and knowledge-graph tutoring; supports bounded domain/context and comparison with non-AI teaching.
limits: Recent single-college anatomy context; intervention bundles AI, graph and instructional model.
